subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Bile is stored in which organ before release into the small intestine?
questions.explain: Bile made in the liver is stored in the gall bladder until needed.

questions.q: Which organ produces amylase, protease and lipase?
questions.explain: The pancreas makes all three types of digestive enzyme and releases them into the small intestine.

questions.q: Which nutrient is the body's main source of energy?
questions.explain: Carbohydrates are the primary energy source in a balanced diet.

questions.q: What is the role of fibre in a balanced diet?
options: Helps food move through the gut and prevents constipation
questions.explain: Dietary fibre is not digested but keeps food moving through the intestines.

questions.q: Where is amylase first produced in the digestive system?
questions.explain: Salivary glands make amylase, which begins starch digestion in the mouth.

questions.q: Which enzyme breaks down starch into sugars?
questions.explain: Amylase is a carbohydrase that digests starch into simple sugars such as maltose.

questions.q: Where is most digested food absorbed into the blood?
questions.explain: The small intestine is adapted with villi to absorb digested food molecules.

questions.q: Why does the large intestine play a role at the end of digestion?
options: It absorbs water from undigested food to form faeces
It absorbs amino acids into the blood
questions.explain: The large intestine absorbs water, leaving solid faeces to be egested.

questions.q: How are villi adapted for absorption?
options: No blood supply to slow diffusion
Large surface area and thin walls with good blood supply
questions.explain: Villi give a large surface area, have thin walls and a rich blood supply for efficient absorption.

questions.q: What does protease break protein down into?
questions.explain: Protease enzymes digest proteins into amino acids.

questions.q: Lipase digests lipids (fats) into which products?
questions.explain: Lipase breaks lipids down into fatty acids and glycerol.
